text: Best Cloud Hosting in 2026: Managed Cloud Plans for Sites That Outgrew Shared Hosting Written by: Rantideb Howlader Rantideb Howlader is HostingGuider’s Technical Analyst, Writer & Researcher, an AWS Certified Solutions Architect and AWS Community Builder with hands-on experience managing cloud infrastructure in production. · Last Updated on: October 18, 2026 · HostingGuider uses affiliate links. We may earn a commission if you purchase through them, at no extra cost to you. ChatGPT Perplexity Gemini Claude Grok Hostinger Cloud Startup is our pick for most sites moving up from shared hosting. It costs $7.99 a month on a 48-month term, then $25.99, for 4 CPU cores, 4 GB of RAM, and 100 PHP workers. We’ve run it for months. Cloudways is the pick if you want to choose your own cloud provider and resize by the hour, from $11 a month. Cloud hosting here means managed cloud: the host runs the server for you, and you get more guaranteed resources than shared hosting. If you’d rather patch and secure a raw server yourself, unmanaged VPS picks sorted by skill and budget cost less each month. Table of Contents What cloud hosting is Cloud hosting runs your site on virtual servers inside a large pool of hardware, so resources can be added or moved without buying a new physical machine. Managed cloud hosting adds a provider who sets up, secures, and maintains that server for you. For your site, this means dedicated CPU and RAM that neighbors can’t take, with less server work than a VPS. The wider set of cloud hosting explainers and scaling guides covers the concepts behind it. The best cloud hosting at a glance Hostinger Cloud Startup: first step up from shared, lowest four-year cost Cloudways: best for choosing your own cloud provider Atlantic.Net : CBest for secure cloud for regulated and business-critical workloads ScalaHosting: best managed cloud with email and a control panel SiteGround Cloud: best for businesses that want phone support Plan CPU RAM Storage Price Four-year cost Backups Refund Current plans Hostinger Cloud Startup 4 cores 4 GB 100 GB NVMe $7.99/mo on 48 months, then $25.99 $383.52 Daily 30 days See Hostinger Cloud plans Cloudways DigitalOcean 4 GB 2 cores 4 GB 80 GB $46/mo, billed hourly $2,208 Offsite storage at $0.033 per GB None listed; 3-day trial See Cloudways plans Atlantic.Net Cloud Server 2 vCPU 4 GB 80 GB NVMe SSD Custom / Usage-Based Varies by Configuration Optional Managed Backups 30 Days See Atlantic.Net Cloud ScalaHosting Build #1 2 cores 4 GB 50 GB NVMe $29.95/mo on 36 months, then $54.95 $1,737.60 Automatic offsite 30 days, full refund See ScalaHosting plans SiteGround Cloud Jump Start 4 cores 8 GB 40 GB SSD $100/mo $4,800 Daily, kept 7 days 14 days See SiteGround plans ScalaHosting’s four-year figure is 36 months at $29.95 plus 12 months at the $54.95 renewal rate. The Hostinger figure covers the 48-month prepaid term only. Plans aren’t identical: SiteGround gives twice the RAM, and Cloudways has no fixed term. Compare them by the resources your site needs, then by price. Cloud plan specs and promo terms shift often, so confirm the core count and term on Hostinger’s cloud plan page at checkout. Each cloud price and spec in the table was read on the host’s own site between September 25 and 28, 2026. How we chose the best cloud hosting We compared managed cloud plans from hosts HostingGuider reviews, at similar resource levels. Guaranteed resources: CPU cores, RAM, and PHP workers, since those decide how many uncached requests a site can handle at once. Four-year cost: intro price, renewal, and billing term. What’s managed: control panel, security updates, and backups. Refunds and trials: how long you have to leave. Our own data: we bought Hostinger Cloud Startup on November 30, 2025, and run our test site on a Singapore server. 1. Hostinger Cloud Startup: first step up from shared hosting Best for: a site that outgrew shared hosting but isn’t ready to run its own server. Skip it if: you need true auto-scaling, or you won’t prepay 48 months for the low price. Cloud Startup gives you 4 CPU cores, 4 GB of RAM, 100 GB of NVMe storage, and 100 PHP workers. Hostinger It includes daily backups, a dedicated IP, a free CDN, and unlimited sites. PHP workers matter more than they sound. Each one handles one uncached request, like a checkout or a logged-in page, at a time. On the Singapore server we’ve used for months, the test site hit PageSpeed 99 on both desktop and mobile. UptimeRobot logged no downtime across 30 days. City Time to first byte Singapore 157 ms Bangalore 247 ms Frankfurt 283 ms Amsterdam 317 ms New York 388 ms London 454 ms San Francisco 515 ms Sydney 674 ms The numbers rise with distance from the server. Across 22 monitoring locations, the average response was about 605 ms with 100% reachability. Those Singapore TTFB and uptime results on Cloud Startup are why it suits Asian and European audiences better than mainly North American ones. Limitation: the price jumps from $7.99 to $25.99 a month at renewal. Our account renews at $311.88 a year. Resources are fixed per plan, so growth means upgrading, not automatic scaling. Visit Hostinger 2. Cloudways: best for choosing your own cloud provider Best for: agencies and technical owners who want to pick DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, AWS, or Google Cloud and resize freely. Skip it if: you want root access, email included, or a money-back guarantee. Cloudways runs managed servers on five clouds and bills by the hour, invoiced monthly, with no contract. Cloudways A 1 GB DigitalOcean server costs $11 a month and a 4 GB server $46. Servers with 2 GB and up include Object Cache Pro free, which helps WooCommerce and membership sites. For a growing site, Cloudways’ hourly billing and provider choice let you size up without a new contract. Limitation: Cloudways doesn’t give root access, lists no uptime SLA or money-back guarantee, and charges for email from $1.50 per mailbox. You get a 3-day free trial instead. Visit Cloudways 3. Atlantic.Net Cloud Server: secure cloud for regulated and business-critical workloads Best for: healthcare, financial services, and SaaS teams that need HIPAA- or PCI DSS-aligned infrastructure with direct engineer access, not just a support ticket queue. Skip it if: you’re comparing purely on price per vCPU, or you’re running a personal project with no compliance requirement. Atlantic.Net’s Cloud Server plan gives you 2 vCPUs, 4 GB of RAM, and 80 GB of NVMe SSD storage, priced on a custom, usage-based model rather than a flat monthly rate. Atlantic.Net Cloud Server secure cloud for regulated and business-critical workloads The company has run infrastructure since 1994, and its support is staffed by engineers rather than a ticket system or community forum, with 24/7 U.S.-based coverage. Atlantic.Net publishes a 100% uptime SLA on its cloud plans, backed by redundant, RAID-protected NVMe storage. It also lists HIPAA and PCI DSS-aligned environments among its offerings, which is relevant if your workload carries a compliance requirement the way a generic cloud VPS usually doesn’t address out of the box. As needs grow, Atlantic.Net’s product line extends into managed services, dedicated servers, private cloud, GPU hosting, and disaster recovery, so a compliance-driven team can expand without re-platforming to a different vendor. Limitation: Atlantic.Net’s usage-based pricing makes it harder to predict a fixed monthly cost compared to flat-rate competitors, and we have not yet run our own hands-on performance test on this plan, so the figures above come from Atlantic.Net’s published specifications rather than independent testing. Visit Atlantic.Net 4. ScalaHosting: best managed cloud with email and a control panel Best for: small businesses that want a managed cloud server with email and backups on one bill. Skip it if: you need cPanel and don’t want to pay for it. ScalaHosting’s managed cloud includes its own SPanel, unlimited email accounts, automatic offsite backups, a dedicated IP, and unmetered bandwidth. ScalaHosting Its entry cloud server, Build #1, pairs 2 cores with 4 GB of RAM and 50 GB of NVMe. New clients who cancel within 30 days get their money back in full. That refund, plus ScalaHosting’s bundled SPanel and mailboxes , lowers the risk of a first cloud move. Email is the dividing line when ScalaHosting and Cloudways compete for the same growing site: one includes it, the other bills per mailbox. Limitation: the $29.95 monthly price needs a 36-month term and rises to $54.95 at renewal. cPanel costs extra, from about $32.95 a month. Visit ScalaHosting 5. SiteGround Cloud: best for businesses that want phone support Best for: established businesses already on SiteGround, or anyone who wants phone support on a managed cloud server. Skip it if: budget matters, or you want backups kept longer than a week. SiteGround’s Jump Start plan gives 4 cores, 8 GB of RAM, 40 GB of SSD, and 5 TB of transfer for $100 a month. siteground Email, staging with Git, and daily backups are included. SiteGround offers 24/7 chat, tickets, and phone, though its help flow may not offer phone for every issue. SiteGround’s support channels and Google Cloud setup suit owners who want a person to call. If you’d rather pay by the hour, SiteGround Cloud and Cloudways differ most on billing and backups. Limitation: it’s the most expensive plan here, cloud backups are kept 7 days instead of the 30 on SiteGround’s shared plans, and the refund window is 14 days. Visit SiteGround Cloud hosting vs VPS hosting Both give you guaranteed resources. The difference is who runs the server and how easily it grows. Managed cloud: the host installs, patches, and backs up the server, often with a control panel. You pay more for less server work. Unmanaged VPS or cloud server: you get root access and do the setup and security yourself. It costs less, but every update is yours. When you need AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure directly Most websites don’t. Hyperscale clouds make sense when you need services beyond a web server, such as managed databases at scale, queues, or multi-region failover, and have an engineer to run them. For a WordPress site or a store, a managed cloud host is usually simpler. Cloudways lets you use AWS or Google Cloud underneath without managing them yourself. Signs you’ve outgrown shared hosting Your shared plan keeps hitting its CPU, RAM, or entry-process ceiling. Checkout, cart, or member pages slow down at busy times. You need more PHP workers for uncached traffic. You want a dedicated IP or more storage than shared plans allow. Other cloud hosts we considered Kinsta: managed WordPress on Google Cloud with 30 data centers. It’s a WordPress-only platform rather than a general cloud server. HostArmada: managed cloud VPS with 5 free cPanel accounts. The first month costs $29.95 on monthly billing, then $59.90, with a 7-day refund. Liquid Web: managed cloud and dedicated hosting for regulated businesses. Its “from” prices are two-month promotions, so check the regular rate. Which cloud host should you choose? Leaving shared hosting, want the lowest four-year cost? Hostinger Cloud Startup. Agency, or want to pick AWS or Google Cloud? Cloudways. Moving critical applications to the cloud and need security and compliance? Atlantic.Net. Business that wants email and a panel included? ScalaHosting. Want phone support and more RAM? SiteGround Cloud. Moving off shared hosting this month? Start with Hostinger Cloud Startup for a fixed plan, or open a Cloudways server you can resize hourly if you expect to grow fast. Frequently asked questions What is managed cloud hosting? It’s a cloud server that the host sets up, secures, and maintains for you. You get dedicated resources without handling the operating system yourself. Is cloud hosting faster than shared hosting? It can be, because your CPU and RAM aren’t shared. In our tests, server location still mattered most: our Singapore cloud server answered in 157 ms locally and 674 ms from Sydney. Is cloud hosting good for eCommerce? Yes, especially for stores with steady traffic. Carts and checkouts can’t be cached, so the extra CPU, RAM, and PHP workers help. Can I scale a cloud hosting plan easily? Usually. Cloudways lets you resize a server and bills by the hour. Hostinger and SiteGround move you to a bigger plan instead of scaling automatically. How much does cloud hosting cost? Managed cloud plans here start at $7.99 a month (Hostinger’s 48-month intro rate) and reach $100 a month for SiteGround Jump Start. Over four years, that’s $383.52 for Hostinger Cloud Startup and $4,800 for SiteGround Jump Start. Which cloud host has the best uptime? Our Hostinger Cloud Startup account held 100% uptime over 30 days. Uptime promises vary, and Cloudways doesn’t list an uptime SLA on its pricing page. How we compared cloud hosting We lined up managed cloud plans at similar RAM and CPU, then read each host’s pricing, backup, and refund terms between September 25 and 28, 2026. Our first-hand data comes from Hostinger Cloud Startup, bought November 30, 2025. Anyone can check the invoice and renewal date for our Cloud Startup plan. We haven’t bought Cloudways, ScalaHosting, or SiteGround Cloud plans. The ranking weighs fit, resources, and four-year cost, in line with how we weigh cost, resources, and support . About The Author Rantideb Howlader is HostingGuider’s Technical Analyst, Writer & Researcher, an AWS Certified Solutions Architect and AWS Community Builder with hands-on experience managing cloud infrastructure in production.

Testing and performance data are collected independently ( see our methodology ). Prices are in USD unless stated otherwise. Table of Content Ask AI about this page: ChatGPT Claude Perplexity Grok Google AI The best managed cloud hosting services deliver high-performance infrastructure, hands-off server management, and support teams that handle the technical heavy lifting for yo u. In our latest performance tests and platform reviews, ScalaHosting leads the field by offering exceptional value, instant scalability, and impressive load performance. Atlantic.Net follows closely as the top choice for enterprises that require strict compliance, hardened security, and 100% uptime guarantees. Cloudways rounds out the top three with its flexible multi-cloud deployment model and beginner-friendly console that simplifies complex infrastructure. Managed cloud hosting removes the burden of configuring servers, manages updates and patches, monitors performance, and automates backups and scaling. It gives businesses the peace of mind that their environment is stable, secured, and properly maintained. For online stores (WooCommerce, PrestaShop), LMS platforms, high-traffic publishers, agency-hosted client sites, and custom applications requiring dependable uptime, managed cloud hosting provides the optimal balance of speed, reliability, and expert support. ScalaHosting Website: https://www.scalahosting.com/managed-cloud-hosting ScalaHosting delivers managed cloud hosting built around simple server management, predictable performance, and long-term scalability. Users can start on ScalaHosting’s native cloud and later move to AWS infrastructure while keeping the same management layer. Its proprietary SPanel control panel also removes cPanel licensing costs and simplifies common workflows for WordPress, ecommerce, and application hosting. Our recent stress tests show that ScalaHosting’s entry managed cloud plan performs well beyond its price tier. The test server sustained 500 concurrent users in one minute with virtually no performance degradation, which is an unusually strong result for this category. With instant server provisioning, server-level security, and beginner-friendly management, ScalaHosting is currently our #1 managed cloud hosting provider with a HostScore of 87.4%. Learn More in Our ScalaHosting Review Scala’s Cloud Hosting Plans & Pricing ScalaHosting’s managed cloud hosting starts at $29.95/mo, offering 2 CPU cores + 4GB memory, SPanel access, daily backups, and full server management. Higher-tier plans expand CPU/RAM allocations and security tooling, with signup priced at $94.95/mo for users who need more compute power. Atlantic.Net Website: https://www.atlantic.net/ Atlantic.Net positions itself as an enterprise-grade cloud hosting provider built for organizations that require strict compliance, high uptime guarantees, and specialized infrastructure. The company supports HIPAA, HITECH, PCI, and SOC requirements across its cloud and dedicated environments, making it a strong fit for regulated industries such as healthcare, finance, and government. Its data centers deliver 100% uptime SLA, and its platform accommodates advanced workloads including GPU-accelerated compute for AI, machine learning, and high-performance computing. While Atlantic.Net’s technology stack is exceptionally powerful, its onboarding process is more traditiona. You’ll need to speak with their team to configure your deployment, which also means pricing is not published upfront. Atlantic.Net Private Cloud Hosting Plans Atlantic.Net structures its managed cloud and compliance-focused hosting through custom quotes. Buyers contact the sales team to define CPU/RAM/storage needs, regulatory requirements, and GPU options, after which a tailored offer is provided. Atlantic.Net Pros & Cons Pros Cons Strong compliance coverage (HIPAA, HITECH, PCI, SOC) Must contact sales to configure/order 100% uptime SLA backed by enterprise-grade facilities Fewer self-service tools Supports GPU workloads (AI, ML, HPC) Less beginner-friendly onboarding Highly secure, enterprise-oriented infrastructure Visit Online 3. Cloudways Website: https://www.cloudways.com/ Cloudways is a user-friendly managed cloud platform that lets developers, agencies, and site owners deploy websites on DigitalOcean , AWS, Google Cloud, Vultr, or Linode without managing the underlying server layer themselves. HostScore.net (this site you are reading) runs on Cloudways, and our experience has been positive, with strong performance and relatively little operational work. The platform uses pay-as-you-go pricing with no setup fees or inflated renewal rates. Core features such as SSL, staging, automated backups, and server-level security are included in the base price, while optional services such as off-site backup storage and premium support tiers can increase the final bill. These extras are listed openly in the dashboard before you commit. The main drawbacks are less technical. Cloudways has become more aggressive in promoting optional add-ons in recent years, and its billing support is noticeably weaker than its technical support team. Learn More in Our Cloudways Review Cloudways Hosting Plans & Pricing Cloudways’ managed cloud hosting uses a pay‑as‑you‑go model and starts at around $11.00 /mo on providers like DigitalOcean and Vultr. Prices increase with server resources and the underlying cloud provider, so higher‑performance AWS or Google Cloud configurations can reach into the high hundreds or even exceed $1,000 per month for very large deployments. Cloudways Autonomous , their autoscaling managed WordPress offering with enhanced performance and WordPress‑specific optimizations, starts at $99/mo, with higher tiers available for larger or more demanding sites. Cloudways Pros & Cons Pros Cons User-friendly managed cloud platform Billing support issues based on our experience Choose from DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, AWS, and Google Cloud Increasingly prominent optional add-ons, though they are clearly listed in the dashboard before you commit Pay-as-you-go billing without higher renewal pricing Malware alerts sometimes produce false positives Cloudways Autonomous automatically scales WordPress resources horizontally during traffic spikes No root access (intentional to the managed hosting model; SSH and SFTP access are still available) Strong agency tools for managing multiple websites, teams, and client projects Visit Online 4. Kinsta Website: https://www.kinsta.com/ Kinsta delivers a premium managed WordPress hosting experience built on Google Cloud Platform’s high-performance infrastructure. Its platform leverages Google’s premium tier network and Cloudflare Enterprise to expand global reach across 300+ CDN locations while strengthening security with advanced firewalls, DDoS mitigation, and automated malware scanning. Kinsta’s MyKinsta dashboard streamlines workflow management with staging, backups, analytics, and developer tooling, making it exceptionally friendly for agencies and power users. With multilingual support teams and a strong focus on performance consistency, the company positions itself as a top-tier solution for mission-critical WordPress environments. Learn More in Our Kinsta Review Kinsta Hosting Managed WP Hosting Plans & Pricing Kinsta’s managed hosting plans start at $35.00/mo, providing one WordPress install with 20GB bandwidth + 10GB storage + 14 days backup retention, Cloudflare Enterprise protection, and fully managed WordPress optimization. Higher-tier plans scale storage, PHP workers, and CDN bandwidth, with signup priced at $675.00/mo. Kinsta Pros & Cons Pros Cons Built on Google Cloud’s premium tier network Pricing is high, especially for multiple small sites Cloudflare Enterprise included No built-in email hosting Advanced security (firewall, DDoS, malware scanning) Certain plugins restricted for performance/security Excellent multilingual support Not ideal for budget-focused users Visit Online 5. LiquidWeb Website: https://www.liquidweb.com/ Liquid Web targets developers, enterprises, and growing businesses that need high availability, strong SLAs, and consistent server performance. With fully owned and self-operated data centers, the company controls every part of its infrastructure, which enhances physical security, network stability, and long-term data integrity. Liquid Web’s cloud platform supports demanding workloads and specialized compliance frameworks (if needed) including PCI and HIPAA. In our recent stress tests on a lower-tier cloud server, Liquid Web delivered excellent load-handling capabilities with predictable throughput and uptime. Its technical depth and enterprise orientation position Liquid Web as a reliable choice for organizations that cannot afford downtime. Learn More in Our LiquidWeb Review LiquidWeb Managed Cloud Hosting Plans & Pricing Liquid Web’s managed cloud plans start at $5.00, offering 6 CPU cores + 16GB memory, managed security, and flexible control panel options (InterWorx or cPanel). LiquidWeb Pros & Cons Pros Cons 100% network uptime SLA No Asia-based data centers Self-owned data centers enhance security and stability Onboarding can be confusing Strong performance in our stress tests Not as beginner-friendly as others PCI- and HIPAA-compliant options available Higher learning curve for small business owners Visit Online 6. Chemicloud Website: https://www.chemicloud.com/ ChemiCloud appeals to small businesses and freelancers needing an affordable starting point in managed cloud hosting. Powered by DigitalOcean’s infrastructure, the platform simplifies deployment through cPanel and offers a clean, beginner-friendly environment for WordPress and general website hosting. The company emphasizes affordability and customer support, making it a practical entry option for users who want managed convenience without the premium cost of enterprise platforms. While it doesn’t deliver the same scalability or compliance capabilities as higher-end providers, ChemiCloud remains one of the better budget-managed cloud hosting choices. Learn More in Our Chemicloud Review ChemiCloud Cloud Hosting Plans & Pricing ChemiCloud’s managed cloud plans range from $32.95 – $194.95 per month, covering a mix of entry-level and mid-tier configurations. All plans include cPanel access, fully managed support, and easy WordPress deployment, with higher tiers expanding CPU/RAM resources for growing sites. Chemicloud Pros & Cons Pros Cons Very affordable entry point for managed cloud Performance not ideal for high-traffic or enterprise workloads Easy to launch with cPanel No PCI/HIPAA compliance options Good for small sites and freelancers Fewer data center choices Strong customer support reputation Visit Online 7. SiteGround Website: https://www.siteground.com/ SiteGround builds its managed cloud hosting on Google Cloud Platform and enhances performance through its proprietary Site Tools control panel and server-level caching technologies. The company delivers exceptional support quality, quick provisioning, and a strong uptime record across its global network. With built-in CDN, automated backups, and security hardening, SiteGround caters to businesses seeking a polished managed hosting experience backed by reliable engineering. However, premium features and GCP-powered performance push prices into a much higher bracket, especially at renewal. Learn More in Our SiteGround Review SiteGround Cloud Hosting Plans & Pricing SiteGround’s managed cloud plans range from $100.00 – $400.00 per month, offering fully managed performance tuning, Site Tools access, and Google Cloud–powered infrastructure. Higher tiers increase CPU cores, RAM, and storage capacity, making them suitable for heavier workloads and fast-growing businesses. SiteGround Pros & Cons Pros Cons Excellent performance with in-house Site Tools Very expensive renewals Built on Google Cloud Platform Some plans still use SSD instead of NVMe Built-in CDN and optimized caching High pricing compared to similar competitors Limited flexibility for advanced users Visit Online Comparison Among the Best Managed Cloud Hosting Services Here’s how our top 7 providers stack up across key decision-making areas: Hosting Provider Starting Price Cloud Infrastructure Control Panel ScalaHosting $29.95/mo AWS / native SPanel Atlantic.Net – Native – (By user choice) Cloudways $11.00/mo DigitalOcean, AWS, GCP, Vultr, Linode Cloudways Console Kinsta $35.00/mo Google Cloud Platform MyKinsta LiquidWeb $5.00/mo Liquid Web Cloud InterWorx / cPanel ChemiCloud $32.95/mo DigitalOcean cPanel SiteGround $100.00/mo Google Cloud Platform Site Tools What’s the Most Beginner-Friendly Managed Cloud Host? SPanel gives users full control over cloud hosting with a lightweight, beginner-friendly interface—no cPanel license required. ScalaHosting is our top recommendation for beginners who want to grow into more advanced features over time. Despite being developer-friendly, ScalaHosting also caters well to non-technical users thanks to its in-house control panel, SPanel. Unlike cPanel, SPanel is lightweight, included at no additional cost, and tailored specifically for cloud VPS users. Here’s why ScalaHosting wins: SPanel includes a visual dashboard, one-click WordPress installer, integrated file manager, email, DNS tools, and staging features — all without needing a separate license. SShield , Scala’s AI-powered security layer, actively monitors threats and blocks 99.998% of attacks based on their internal metrics. Customer support is highly rated, offering 24/7 live chat with fast, technical responses—something we confirmed in our user tests. Convincing performance in our load tests — Scala’s cloud hosting consistently maintained sub-150ms response times and handled 1,000+ concurrent users on entry-level plans with little degradation. Starting at $29.95/mo , it offers an excellent value for managed cloud hosting, making it both accessible and scalable. If you’re just starting out and want a managed hosting experience that doesn’t overwhelm you and without overpaying – ScalaHosting is a strong choice. Which Managed Cloud Provider is Best for Online Stores? Cloudways optimizes performance with built-in caching layers, PHP-FPM, PHP 8 ready hosting, , auto-healing servers, and advanced server-level controls. Cloudways is the most versatile choice for online stores, especially those powered by WooCommerce. With dedicated server resources, built-in object caching (Memcached + Redis), and vertical scaling, Cloudways ensures your store stays fast. For high-growth or enterprise ecommerce setups, Kinsta is a premium alternative. It uses Google Cloud C2 instances, optimized for database-heavy applications like WooCommerce, and includes automatic scaling and server-level caching. What’s the Most Scalable Managed Cloud Platform? With over 35 global data center locations, Kinsta lets you host your site closer to your audience for faster performance and lower latency. Kinsta is the most scalable managed cloud hosting platform for users who prioritize global reach and consistent performance. Built entirely on Google Cloud Platform’s premium-tier network, Kinsta leverages C2 virtual machines across 35+ server locations worldwide. This setup allows users to deploy their websites closer to their audience, reducing latency and improving load speeds across regions. Kinsta’s infrastructure also supports auto-scaling, making it ideal for high-traffic websites and eCommerce stores that experience unpredictable spikes. For users who prefer raw scalability and infrastructure-level control, Kamatera and LiquidWeb are solid alternatives. Kamatera offers near-instant vertical and horizontal scaling with granular resource control, while LiquidWeb provides enterprise-grade managed cloud VPS and dedicated resources that are ideal for mission-critical workloads. Which Managed Cloud Provider is Best for Hosting Resellers? ScalaHosting is our top pick for resellers thanks to its white-labeling support built into every managed VPS plan. Users can rebrand SPanel, assign their own nameservers, and create isolated accounts for each clien without needing WHM/cPanel licenses. Key features include: Reseller-friendly billing options and multi-user account support Built-in SShield and automated backups for client sites No extra cost for SPanel or white-label features Support for unlimited websites and client accounts on higher-tier plans If you’re a web designer, agency, or small hosting startup, ScalaHosting offers the tools and flexibility to run your business under your own brand. Which Managed Cloud Provider is Best for Agencies? Both Cloudways and Kinsta cater exceptionally well to agency workflows. Cloudways supports team-based access, app-level controls, and Git/SFTP integration. Agencies can deploy apps across multiple cloud providers, assign different roles to collaborators, and clone/stage projects easily. The billing is monthly, transparent, and suitable for managing dozens of client sites. Kinsta provides robust team collaboration tools and client hand-off features via MyKinsta, their clean and intuitive dashboard. Automatic scalability, 35+ data center locations, and enterprise-grade security make it ideal for agencies working with premium clients. If your agency needs flexibility and control, Cloudways is more customizable. If you’re serving corporate or high-value clients, Kinsta offers polish and performance. How is Managed Cloud Hosting Different from Unmanaged Hosting? Managed cloud hosting works by combining cloud-based infrastructure with expert server management, so your hosting provider handles technical tasks like setup, security, updates, and performance optimization while you focus on running your website. The main difference between managed and unmanaged cloud hosting lies in who handles the technical responsibilities. In Managed Cloud Hosting, the provider takes care of all the technical details. This includes server setup, regular updates, security measures, and providing support whenever you need it. It’s like having a dedicated IT team without the overhead costs. In comparison, Unmanaged Cloud Hosting places the responsibility squarely on your shoulders. You’re responsible for everything: From setting up the server to maintaining it, installing updates, and troubleshooting any issues that arise. While this option offers more control, it also requires a higher level of technical expertise and time commitment. Feature Managed Cloud Hosting Unmanaged Cloud Hosting Management Provider handles setup, maintenance, monitoring, and security. User is responsible for all server management tasks. Support Comprehensive 24/7 support and assistance with server-related issues. Limited support, often restricted to hardware and network-related issues. Security Advanced security measures and regular updates handled by the provider. User must implement and maintain security measures. Cost Generally more expensive due to additional services and support. Typically cheaper, but additional costs for managing and securing the server. Flexibility Less control over server configurations. More control and flexibility in configuring the server to meet specific requirements. Pros & Cons of Managed Cloud Hosting Pros Cons Less Maintenance – Server updates, patches, and security configurations are handled by experts. Vendor Lock-in – Migration can be tricky due to proprietary control panels or configurations. Improved Performance – Managed environments are often optimized at the OS and app layer. Higher Cost – Managed hosting is more expensive than shared or unmanaged VPS. Better Support – Access to specialized support teams trained in WordPress, Magento, WooCommerce, etc. Less Control – You may not have full root access or be able to customize every system-level setting. Security Built-in – Firewalls, malware scanning, and DDoS protection are often part of the package. Easy Backups & Restores – Most platforms include daily backups with one-click restore options. Final Thoughts Managed cloud hosting has evolved into an essential solution for site owners who want top-tier performance without the hassle of server administration. Whether you’re running a growing online store, managing client sites, or launching a global content platform, the providers we’ve highlighted offer a range of features tailored to different needs. From ScalaHosting’s user-friendly SPanel and reseller tools to Kinsta’s premium Google Cloud infrastructure and Cloudways’ flexible deployment options, there’s a managed cloud host here for every stage of your growth. text: Cloud service providers: Top clouds and how to choose your cloud provider Choosing the right cloud hosting solutions for your business, website, or application is a critical decision. Below we’ll walk you through the top cloud providers today and how to compare their benefits and features. Sign up for DigitalOcean today What is a cloud provider? Cloud providers refer to businesses that offer cloud computing services such as cloud infrastructure (including virtual machines and virtual private servers , databases , cloud storage , and more to users who want to host websites and applications in the cloud. Cloud providers offer multiple services distributed across a network of data centers, usually located around the world. Cloud providers are an alternative to traditional on-premise hosting infrastructure, which has declined in usage due to the easily accessible and affordable nature of cloud hosting solutions. Some of the largest cloud providers offer hundreds of products, but the most commonly used cloud services include: Infrastructure as a Service, Platform as a Service, Databases, Storage, Kubernetes, Serverless/Functions. Top cloud providers The top cloud providers by market share, often referred to as hyperscaler clouds , are Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure. AWS is the largest cloud provider, but many businesses look for AWS alternatives as AWS can be very complex, especially for the needs of individual developers and small businesses, and their pricing can be expensive when factoring in AWS egress costs . Smaller clouds like DigitalOcean offer reliable cloud hosting that is simpler to use and often more cost-effective than the big three clouds—learn how DigitalOcean compares to AWS and Google Cloud Platform . DigitalOcean is the comprehensive agentic cloud, empowering developers at AI-native businesses and digital native enterprises to build full-stack AI applications with straightforward tools, transparent pricing, and developer-friendly features and documentation. Sign up today to get started. How to choose between cloud providers When comparing cloud providers, you should consider several factors, including price, global data center locations, products, customer support, documentation, and more. A cloud provider is typically a long-term commitment—while businesses can switch cloud service providers, the process can be time-consuming and expensive, so choosing the right cloud provider from the start will set you up for success. Pricing Consider cost, including both base product pricing, egress pricing (also known as bandwidth or data transfer fees), and additional pricing for add-ons like support. Certain cloud providers like AWS are known for their pricing complexity, so understanding how prices break down and will scale as you grow is important. DigitalOcean pricing Product offerings Most cloud providers offer some sort of virtual machine or VPS hosting, though some may only offer shared hosting services, which are more suitable for low-traffic websites. Many cloud providers will also offer managed databases, storage, load balancing, Kubernetes, and other products that may be part of your long-term infrastructure. Research what you’ll need and choose a cloud provider that offers those products. DigitalOcean products Support Support is a critical but often overlooked component of choosing any vendor, and choosing a cloud provider is no different. Many cloud providers don’t offer free support beyond billing questions, while some like DigitalOcean offer free ticketed support for all users, and low monthly-cost options for more robust support plans with faster response times. DigitalOcean Support Plans Data center locations It’s important to consider where the majority of your users will be located when accessing your website or application when choosing a cloud service provider. Most larger cloud providers have a network of global data centers, but may have gaps in certain locations. DigitalOcean data centers Documentation In addition to ticketed support, documentation is also important for self-diagnosing a problem with your cloud infrastructure. Look into product documentation, community forums, instructional tutorials, and more before deciding what cloud service provider to use. DigitalOcean documentation Supported operating systems While most cloud providers support Linux operating systems, some like Microsoft Azure also offer Windows-based virtual machines. Know what operating system and distribution, such as Ubuntu 22.04, you plan to use to ensure your chosen cloud provider can support it. Some cloud providers also offer tutorials on how to install and manage operating systems. Read article Article AWS alternatives Read article Frequently Asked Questions What is cloud computing? Cloud computing provides cloud services, including cloud infrastructure such as servers, cloud storage, databases, and more, virtually via an internet connection, so that websites and applications do not need to own and manage their own servers or data centers. Cloud computing makes it extremely easy for anyone to get access to cloud infrastructure at a low cost and without the overhead required for setting up physical servers. There are many cloud computing providers today, with some of the largest including Google Cloud Platform, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Alibaba Cloud for the Chinese cloud market, Microsoft Azure, Dell Technologies Cloud, and IBM Cloud. Smaller providers like DigitalOcean also provide cloud computing services tailored to the needs of specific groups, such as small businesses and startups. The cloud infrastructure market has grown hugely over the past decade, and cloud service providers now have a combined market size of over $569 billion dollars in 2022 . What is the difference between infrastructure as a service, platform as a service, and software as a service? Infrastructure as a service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS) and Software as a service (SaaS) are different services that are often provided by one cloud service provider. IaaS is a type of cloud computing that gives users complete control over their virtual server or infrastructure configuration, without having to manage the underlying physical servers. Platform as a Service allows users to build applications without managing the operating system, runtime, or other infrastructure components of their server. SaaS are very common, and give users an interface to work with without needing to configure any backend technology - many emerging technologies are built as SaaS tools, such as those which allow you to view customer data, send emails, or conduct other regular business processes such as marketing and sales. How do I choose a cloud service provider? There are many cloud service providers out there, from large public clouds like Google Cloud, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, to regional or more niche cloud service providers who focus on a specific region or type of cloud computing. Cloud providers like DigitalOcean give users a range of services including managed services such as managed databases and managed Kubernetes, virtual machines or virtual private servers, managed web hosting through Cloudways by DigitalOcean, and even GPUs for artificial intelligence computing services from Paperspace by DigitalOcean. Should I choose a public cloud, private cloud, hybrid cloud, or multi-cloud service provider? There are multiple options available for a new application or website looking to choose a cloud service provider. When thinking about cloud computing, most businesses today will use public cloud services, though some large enterprises may create a private cloud where they utilize their own data centers and on-premises hardware. A private cloud is usually not the first choice for smaller businesses, who can benefit from the easily accessible cloud computing services available from public cloud service providers. Hybrid cloud models mean that the user both uses a public cloud service provider and also some on-premises data center servers, and may be used if a business has a specific need for some on-premises servers. What are the top cloud service providers? The top cloud service providers include Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure Cloud, Google Cloud Platform , the third largest hosting company. While these three cloud service providers are the top by market share, there are many other cloud services providers that offer similar services, often with less complexity, a smaller range of products, and sometimes a lower cost. DigitalOcean is an excellent alternative to these three top cloud service providers, as it offers many cloud computing services, including CPU compute, databases, GPUs to support artificial intelligence, and Kubernetes, but has lower bandwidth costs and more simple services than many larger providers. Other alternative cloud platforms include IMB Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and Dell Technologies Cloud service provider. All of these providers offer a range of cloud resources and cloud based services, but have differences in the specific services they offer, cloud costs, data center locations, and more.
